evals.name: pricing-untested-branches
evals.prompt: Review the tests in this change for quality before I merge it. The change is in pricing.py (adds a bulk discount tier and fixes an empty-cart crash) and its tests are in test_pricing.py. Both files are in the folder I gave you. Are these tests actually good enough, and would they catch a regression? Give me a proper test review.
evals.expected_output: Identifies: empty-cart branch untested (the fix itself), bulk-discount >=10 boundary untested, HALF discount code untested, and the vacuous `assert result is not None` assertion. Uses the Test Reviewer template with a coverage map. Verdict Request changes.

evals.name: dateutil-brittle-tests
evals.prompt: Can you look at session.test.js and tell me if the tests are any good? The code under test is session.js (session-expiry helpers). I'm worried these tests are flaky. Do a testing review.
evals.expected_output: Flags brittleness: wall-clock `new Date()` dependence, exact float equality `toBe(30)`, and time-drift concerns. Flags vacuous `expect(result).toBeDefined()`. Notes missing boundary (exactly at ttl, > vs >=) and missing minutesRemaining-clamps-to-0 case. Uses the template.

evals.name: notifier-uncovered-failure-modes
evals.prompt: Review PR test coverage for notifier.py and test_notifier.py in the folder I shared. This PR added retry logic and error handling. Are the important paths tested? Write up a test review I can paste on the PR.
evals.expected_output: Identifies uncovered failure modes: retry-on-ConnectionError path untested, NotificationError-after-all-retries untested, empty-message skip (returns False) untested. Flags over-mocking (asserts mock called, not that the correct payload/user was posted). Uses the template with coverage map. Verdict Request changes.
